title: “Our Neighbourhood”; or, Sketches in the Suburbs of Yedo
summary: Twenty-one short sketches of life in a village on the edge of Yedo (Tokyo) in the early 1870s, written by a foreign resident who signs himself “T. A. P.” and writes as one of the neighbourhood. They were first printed in the Japan Weekly Mail and collected in Yokohama in 1874. Each describes a person, a trade, or a custom: the saké shop, the stone mason, the barber and the stories told in his shop, a blind boy, a picker-up of paper scraps, a shrine festival, the sparrow catcher, the doctor, the fortune-teller, the story-teller, a flute player, temple bells, an old gate, and the graveyard. The tone is light and often humorous. Japanese words are given in italics. The book has 24 full-page woodcuts in a Japanese style.
